text:
Consider a block kept on an inclined plane (incline at 45${}^{\circ }$) as shown in the figure. If the force required to just push it up the incline is 2 times the force required to just prevent it from sliding down, the coefficient of friction between the block and inclined plane($μ$) is equal to :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

To just push the block up, friction acts down the incline with its limiting value $μN=μmg\cos 45^{\circ }$:

$F_{1}=mg\sin 45^{\circ }+μmg\cos 45^{\circ }=\dfrac{mg}{\sqrt{2}}(1+μ)$


[IMG]

To just prevent sliding down, friction acts up the incline:

$F_{2}=mg\sin 45^{\circ }-μmg\cos 45^{\circ }=\dfrac{mg}{\sqrt{2}}(1-μ)$

Given $F_{1}=2F_{2}$:

$1+μ=2(1-μ)\Rightarrow 3μ=1\Rightarrow μ=\dfrac{1}{3}\approx 0.33$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift

text:
Every planet revolves around the sun in an elliptical orbit :-

A. The force acting on a planet is inversely proportional to square of distance from sun.

B. Force acting on planet is inversely proportional to product of the masses of the planet and the sun.

C. The Centripetal force acting on the planet is directed away from the sun.

D. The square of time period of revolution of planet around sun is directly proportional to cube of semi-major axis of elliptical orbit.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A. The force acting on a planet is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the sun. This is known as the inverse square law and is described by Newton's law of gravitation.

B. Force acting on a planet is inversely proportional to the product of the masses of the planet and the sun. This is also described by Newton's law of gravitation, but it is not directly related to the planet's elliptical orbit.

C. The centripetal force acting on the planet is directed towards the sun, not away from it.

D. The square of the time period of revolution of a planet around the sun is directly proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis of the elliptical orbit. This is known as Kepler's third law.

Therefore, only A and D are correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift

$\mathrm{R}_{1}=\frac{\mathrm{u}^{2}\sin 2α}{\mathrm{g}}$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{R}_{2}=\dfrac{\mathrm{u}^{2}\sin 2β}{\mathrm{g}} \\  \\ α+β=90^{\circ }(\text{Given}) \\  \\ \Rightarrow β=90^{\circ }-α \\  \\ \mathrm{R}_{2}=\dfrac{\mathrm{u}^{2}\sin 2(90^{\circ }-α)}{\mathrm{g}} \\  \\ \mathrm{R}_{2}=\dfrac{\mathrm{u}^{2}\sin (180^{\circ }-2α)}{\mathrm{g}} \\  \\ \mathrm{R}_{2}=\dfrac{\mathrm{u}^{2}\sin 2α}{\mathrm{g}} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{\mathrm{R}_{1}}{\mathrm{R}_{2}}=\dfrac{\left (\frac{\mathrm{u}^{2}\sin 2α}{\mathrm{g}}\right )}{\left (\frac{\mathrm{u}^{2}\sin 2α}{\mathrm{g}}\right )}=\dfrac{1}{1} \end{array}$

text:
Statement I : When a Si sample is doped with Boron, it becomes P type and when doped by Arsenic it becomes N-type semi conductor such that P-type has excess holes and N-type has excess electrons.

Statement II : When such P-type and N-type semi-conductors, are fused to make a junction, a current will automatically flow which can be detected with an externally connected ammeter.

In the light of above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both Statement I and statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Boron is trivalent (acceptor), so boron-doped Si is p-type with holes as majority carriers; arsenic is pentavalent (donor), so arsenic-doped Si is n-type with electrons as majority carriers. Statement I is correct.

When the two are joined, holes and electrons diffuse across the junction only until the depletion layer and its barrier potential are built up; then the drift current equals the diffusion current and the net current across the junction is zero.

With an external ammeter connected, the contact potentials around the closed circuit cancel the barrier potential, so no steady current flows and the ammeter reads zero. Statement II is incorrect.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift

The energy levels of an atom is shown in figure.

Which one of these transitions will result in the emission of a photon of wavelength 124.1 nm?

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The emitted wavelength is $λ=\dfrac{hc}{\Delta E}$, with $hc=\dfrac{6.62\times 10^{-34}\times 3\times 10^{8}}{1.6\times 10^{-19}}\text{eV m}\approx 1241\text{eV nm}$.

Energy gaps from the figure: A ($0\to -2.2$ eV) $2.2$ eV, B ($0\to -5.2$ eV) $5.2$ eV, C ($-2.2\to -5.2$ eV) $3.0$ eV, D ($0\to -10.0$ eV) $10.0$ eV.

Wavelengths: $λ_{A}=\dfrac{1241}{2.2}=564\text{nm}$, $λ_{B}=\dfrac{1241}{5.2}=239\text{nm}$, $λ_{C}=\dfrac{1241}{3}=414\text{nm}$, $λ_{D}=\dfrac{1241}{10}=124.1\text{nm}$.

So transition D emits the 124.1 nm photon, and transition D is listed as option (D).

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
Two long parallel wires carrying currents 8A and 15A in opposite directions are placed at a distance of 7 cm from each other. A point P is equidistant from both the wires such that the lines joining the point P to the wires are perpendicular to each other. The magnitude of magnetic field at P is $_____________$ $\times 10^{-6}$ T.

(Given : $\sqrt{2}=1.4$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Both wires are perpendicular to the plane of the figure; in this cross-section they appear as two points $7\text{cm}$ apart, and P lies in the same plane.


[IMG]

P is equidistant from the two wires and the lines joining P to them are perpendicular, so P and the two wires form a right isosceles triangle with hypotenuse $7\text{cm}$:

$d=\dfrac{7}{\sqrt{2}}\text{cm}=\dfrac{7}{1.4}\text{cm}=5\text{cm}$

The field of each wire at P is perpendicular to the line joining that wire to P. These two lines are perpendicular, so the two fields are perpendicular to each other:

$B_{1}=\dfrac{μ_{0}i_{1}}{2πd},B_{2}=\dfrac{μ_{0}i_{2}}{2πd}$

$B=\sqrt{B_{1}^{2}+B_{2}^{2}}=\dfrac{μ_{0}}{2πd}\sqrt{8^{2}+15^{2}}=\dfrac{2\times 10^{-7}\times 17}{5\times 10^{-2}}\text{T}$

$B=6.8\times 10^{-5}\text{T}=68\times 10^{-6}\text{T}$

Hence, the answer is 68.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift

When half filled with $K=1.5$

From (1) & (2)

$C_{\mathrm{eq}}=\left (\frac{2\times 1.5}{1.5+1}\right )5μ\mathrm{F}=6μ\mathrm{F}$

text: A series LCR circuit is connected to an AC source of 220 V, 50 Hz. The circuit contains a resistance R = 80$\Omega$, an inductor of inductive reactance $\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}=70\Omega$, and a capacitor of capacitive reactance $\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}}=130\Omega$. The power factor of circuit is $\frac{x}{10}$. The value of $x$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \cos 𝜙=\dfrac{\mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{Z}}=\dfrac{\mathrm{R}}{\sqrt{\mathrm{R}^{2}+(\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}}-\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}})^{2}}} \\  \\ \cos 𝜙=\dfrac{80}{\sqrt{(80)^{2}+(60)^{2}}} \\  \\ \cos 𝜙=\dfrac{80}{100}\Rightarrow \dfrac{8}{10} \end{array}$

So, $x=8$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift

text: If a solid sphere of mass 5 kg and a disc of mass 4 kg have the same radius. Then the ratio of moment of inertia of the disc about a tangent in its plane to the moment of inertia of the sphere about its tangent will be $\frac{x}{7}$. The value of $x$ is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:

$\begin{array}{l} I_{\text{tangent}}=I_{\mathrm{cm}}+mR^{2} \\  \\ =\dfrac{2}{5}mR^{2}+mR^{2}=\dfrac{7}{5}mR^{2} \\  \\ =7R^{2}(m=5\mathrm{kg}) \end{array}$

CIRCULAR DISC :

$\frac{I_{\text{disc}}}{I_{\text{tangent}}}=\frac{5}{7}$

text: A body of mass 1 kg collides head on elastically with a stationary body of mass 3 kg. After collision, the smaller body reverses its direction of motion and moves with a speed of 2 m/s. The initial speed of the smaller body before collision is $___________ ms{}^{-1}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Before collision


[IMG]


After collision

Momentum conservation

u + 0 = 3 v – 2 

3v - u = 2    …(1)

also,

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{v+2}{u}=1\Rightarrow v+2=u \\  \\ u-v=2....(2) \end{array}$

Adding (1) and (2)

$\begin{array}{l} 2v=4 \\  \\ v=2\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s} \\  \\ \therefore u=4\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s} \end{array}$

text: A spherical drop of liquid splits into 1000 identical spherical drops. If u${}_{\mathrm{i}}$ is the surface energy of the original drop and u${}_{\mathrm{f}}$ is the total surface energy of the resulting drops, then (ignoring evaporation), $\frac{u_{f}}{u_{i}}=\left (\frac{10}{x}\right )$. Then value of x is $____________$ :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Surface Tension $=\mathrm{T}$

$\mathrm{R}$ : Radius of bigger drop

$\mathrm{r}$ : Radius of smaller drop

Volume will remain same

$\frac{4}{3}πR^{3}=1000\times \frac{4}{3}πr^{3}$

$\mathrm{R}=10\mathrm{r}$

$\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{i}}=\mathrm{T}\cdot 4π\mathrm{R}^{2}$

$\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{f}}=\mathrm{T}.4π\mathrm{r}^{2}\times 1000$

$\frac{\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{i}}}=\frac{1000\mathrm{r}^{2}}{\mathrm{R}^{2}}$

$\frac{\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{i}}}=\frac{10}{1}$

So, $x=1$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift
